# Report: Does Drinking Boiled Garlic Water Cure COVID-19?

**Conclusion: The claim is FALSE. There is no scientific evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19.**

## Evidence Summary

The claim that boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 emerged early in the pandemic and has been repeatedly debunked by health authorities and fact-checkers. AFP Fact Check reported as early as February 2020 that health professionals found no evidence supporting garlic as an effective COVID-19 treatment (https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19).

FactCheck.org similarly addressed this misinformation, classifying garlic among "fake coronavirus cures" and confirming it is not a cure for the disease (https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/).

The World Health Organization has explicitly addressed garlic-related COVID-19 myths through its Mythbusters series, noting there is currently no licensed medication to cure COVID-19 and advising the public to seek information from healthcare professionals rather than unverified remedies (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters).

While garlic does possess some general antiviral properties demonstrated in laboratory studies, research published in PubMed shows these are prophylactic effects against viral infections broadly—not specific evidence against COVID-19 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32836826/). Health authorities emphasize that garlic's general health benefits are not a substitute for targeted antiviral therapies or vaccines.

**Bottom line:** Rely on proven preventive measures and consult healthcare professionals for COVID-19 treatment rather than unverified home remedies.
